subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: What permanent contract should `clawhub skill publish --source-*` provide: documentation-only non-visible metadata, separately displayed unverified attribution, or a new server-verified publish workflow?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the intentional security boundary but cannot determine whether accepted client metadata should remain hidden, become visibly untrusted, or trigger substantial server-side verification.

options.title: Document Current Boundary
options.body: Keep client source claims outside public and trusted provenance, clarify this in CLI help and docs, and consider deprecating flags that have no supported visible effect.

options.title: Expose Unverified Attribution
options.body: Store and display the publisher claim under an unmistakably unverified field that never affects verify results, skill-card trust, or installation decisions.

options.title: Verify CLI Sources
options.body: Add server-side repository, commit, path, ownership, and uploaded-content validation before creating trusted sourceProvenance.

recommendation.title: Document Current Boundary
recommendation.body: Keep client source claims outside public and trusted provenance, clarify this in CLI help and docs, and consider deprecating flags that have no supported visible effect.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged GitHub-backed source work provides the closest concrete ownership and architectural context for this trust-contract decision.
